explanation: N1490+ is a layer-0 lexical (unigram) detector: the positive pole is a fixed function of the current token string alone, so one string gives one strength in every context, position and language (' field' = 0.61 in five different sentences across two languages, ' military' = 0.63, ' theta' = 0.46, 'ن' = 0.77) and no earlier or later token changes it. Its trigger set is a closed, learned ~5% slice of the vocabulary (about 2,400 of 50,304 strings, each with its own fixed strength), densest on individual Greek-letter/notation tokens ('theta', 'eta', 'psi', 'phi', 'Delta', 'Gamma', 'Sigma', 'omega', 'xi', 'lambda', 'nabla', 'vartheta', 'varphi') and on single-token Latinate technical words and English name/place strings (' technical', 'param', 'checkpoint', 'military', 'radio', 'field', 'simpler', 'complex', ' Hay', ' Ma', 'Jackson'), while function words, ordinary nouns and plurals, other learned vocabulary ('hypothesis', 'algorithm', 'paradigm') and the non-member Greek letters ('tau', 'pi', 'epsilon', 'kappa') stay inactive; strength follows the token string rather than the word, since a word's case and space variants carry their own values ('omega' 0.56 but ' omega' 0.04).
